unit.label: Diagnosis & treatment
unit.title: Diagnosis, Medicine, and Treatment
unit.description: Identify illness, discuss medicine and recovery, and use introductory 把.

banner.pinyin: Qǐngwèn wǒ děi chī yào ma?

goal.text: 回去把藥吃了，多喝水，多休息。
goal.pinyin: Huíqù bǎ yào chī le, duō hē shuǐ, duō xiūxí.
goal.meaning: Go back and take the medicine, drink more water, and rest more.

lessons.title: It Is a Cold
lessons.subtitle: Identify the illness as a cold.

steps.prompt: 感冒 means…
steps.explanation: 感冒 gǎnmào means to have/catch a cold.

steps.prompt: Which sentence identifies the illness as a cold?
steps.explanation: 是感冒 identifies the illness as a cold.

steps.prompt: What diagnosis do you hear?
steps.explanation: The diagnosis is 感冒.

lessons.title: Not Anything Specific
lessons.subtitle: Add the non-interrogative 幾 sense and the negative non-specific question-word pattern.

steps.prompt: Which use of 幾 is the new sense taught here?
options: 幾 = a few/several in a statement
steps.answer: 幾 = a few/several in a statement
steps.explanation: Unit 46 adds the non-interrogative few/several sense.

steps.prompt: Which sentence uses a question word inside a negative statement to mean something non-specific?
steps.explanation: The negative non-specific question-word pattern uses a question word inside a negative declarative without requiring 都/也.

steps.prompt: What restriction applies to these non-specific question-word statements?
steps.explanation: The rule states the non-committal statements are always negative.

steps.prompt: Which sentence uses the earlier question-word + 都 totality pattern instead?
steps.explanation: 都 marks the earlier totality pattern.

steps.prompt: Why is 沒有什麼關係 an example of the negative non-specific question-word pattern?
options: 什麼 appears in a negative non-specific statement
什麼 asks a literal information question
steps.answer: 什麼 appears in a negative non-specific statement
steps.explanation: 沒有 supplies the negative environment required by the rule.

lessons.title: Medicine and the Pharmacy
lessons.subtitle: Talk about medicine, pharmacy actions, and modal 得.

steps.prompt: 藥 means…
steps.explanation: 藥 means medicine.

steps.prompt: 藥局 means…
steps.explanation: 藥局 means pharmacy.

steps.prompt: 拿 means…
steps.explanation: 拿 means get.

steps.prompt: In 我得吃藥, 得 is pronounced and understood as…
steps.explanation: This is modal 得, introduced here as support.

steps.prompt: Which translation matches 請問我得吃藥嗎？
options: Do I have to take medicine?
How many medicines did I buy?
steps.answer: Do I have to take medicine?
steps.explanation: 得 děi expresses necessity.

steps.prompt: Where should the person go?
steps.explanation: The instruction says to go to the pharmacy to get medicine.

lessons.title: The 把 Construction
lessons.subtitle: Use the carefully constrained introductory 把 pattern.

steps.prompt: 別 means…
steps.explanation: 別 bié is imperative negation.

steps.prompt: Under the introductory 把 pattern, which sentence is correct?
steps.explanation: The model uses a definite/referential object and an allowed outward action.

steps.prompt: Which verb can be used as the bare action verb here?
steps.explanation: The The pattern models outward actions such as 吃/喝/寫/賣.

steps.prompt: Where does 沒 go in a negative 把 sentence under this pattern?
steps.explanation: Negation precedes 把.

steps.prompt: Which imperative has the correct negation order?
steps.explanation: 別 comes before 把.

steps.prompt: Which question correctly uses the 把 pattern taught here?
steps.explanation: The pattern uses 了沒有 or 是不是 questions.

steps.prompt: Why is the final 了 retained in 我沒把豬腳麵線吃了？
options: This lesson is treating that 了 as sentence-final in the introductory 把 pattern.
steps.answer: This lesson is treating that 了 as sentence-final in the introductory 把 pattern.
steps.explanation: This contrasts this with prior verbal-了.

steps.prompt: Which word gives the negative command?
steps.explanation: 別 means “don't.”

steps.prompt: 水 means…
steps.explanation: 水 means water.

steps.prompt: 休息 means…
steps.explanation: 休息 means rest.

steps.prompt: 睡覺 means…
steps.explanation: 睡覺 is shuìjiào; 覺 is read jiào here.

steps.prompt: 早一點 means…
steps.explanation: 早一點 means a bit earlier.

steps.prompt: In 多休息, 多 expresses…
steps.explanation: this lesson extends prior 多 + V into health advice.

steps.prompt: Which advice tells the patient to sleep a little earlier?
steps.explanation: 早一點 modifies the sleep time.

steps.audioText: 多喝水，多休息，早一點睡覺。
steps.prompt: Which three kinds of advice do you hear?
options: drink more water, rest more, sleep earlier
buy medicine, go home, eat less
steps.answer: drink more water, rest more, sleep earlier
steps.explanation: These are the three advice phrases in the audio.

lessons.title: The Doctor Visit
lessons.subtitle: Integrate the rest of the doctor visit and apply the 把 pattern in three responses.

steps.prompt: In 謝謝您, 您 is…
steps.explanation: 您 nín is polite “you.” It remains support-only.

steps.prompt: What do all three practice responses have in common?
options: doing something with/to a salient object using 把
steps.answer: doing something with/to a salient object using 把
steps.explanation: They all practice doing something with or to a salient object using 把.

steps.prompt: What is the patient asking?
options: whether they have to take medicine
steps.answer: whether they have to take medicine
steps.explanation: 得 děi expresses necessity.

steps.prompt: Which place is named?
steps.explanation: The audio names the pharmacy.

steps.audioText: 多喝水，多休息，早一點睡覺。
steps.prompt: Which item is NOT part of the advice?
steps.explanation: The complete advice is to drink more water, rest more, and sleep earlier.

steps.prompt: 感冒 means…
steps.explanation: 感冒 means have a cold.

steps.prompt: 藥 means…
steps.explanation: 藥 means medicine.

steps.prompt: 藥局 means…
steps.explanation: 藥局 means pharmacy.

steps.prompt: 拿 means…
steps.explanation: 拿 means get.

steps.prompt: 把 means…
steps.explanation: 把 is the disposal marker.

steps.prompt: 別 means…
steps.explanation: 別 means don't.

steps.prompt: 水 means…
steps.explanation: 水 means water.

steps.prompt: 休息 means…
steps.explanation: 休息 means rest.

steps.prompt: Which pronunciation/meaning matches 睡覺?
steps.explanation: 覺 is jiào in 睡覺.

steps.prompt: 早一點 means…
steps.explanation: 早一點 means a bit earlier.

steps.prompt: Which is the expanded use of 幾 taught here?
steps.explanation: The new sense is taught locally without duplicate Search/Mega ownership.

steps.prompt: Which sentence is a negative non-specific question-word statement rather than the earlier totality pattern?
steps.explanation: This is a negative non-specific declarative.

steps.prompt: What is required in the negative non-specific question-word pattern taught here?
steps.explanation: The rule says these statements are always negative.

steps.explanation: 別 precedes 把.

steps.explanation: 是不是 is a supported question route.

steps.prompt: Which pairing is correct?
options: 得 děi + V = must; V 得 de + state = performance complement
得 de + V = must; 得 děi always marks comparison
得 has only one reading here
steps.answer: 得 děi + V = must; V 得 de + state = performance complement
steps.explanation: Modal 得 and complement 得 are distinct.

steps.prompt: Which pair describes a runny nose and poor appetite?
steps.explanation: This retrieves Unit-45 symptom language.

steps.prompt: Which is the Unit-45 duration exchange?
options: 大概多久了？／已經四、五天了。
steps.answer: 大概多久了？／已經四、五天了。
steps.explanation: This is delayed retrieval of the duration-to-now question and answer.

newVocabulary.note: A common cold; used as a verb for catching or having one.
Medicine. Say 吃藥 chī yào for “take medicine,” even though 吃 usually means “eat.”
A pharmacy or drugstore where you get medicine. 藥 means medicine.
To take, hold, or get something. 拿藥 means to collect or get medicine.
Marks the affected object before the action: 把藥吃了, “take the medicine.” It has no separate English translation in this pattern.
Put before an action to tell someone not to do it. This is the imperative “don’t,” not the “other” sense.
Water as a drink here. 多喝水 means “drink more water.”
To rest or take a break. 多休息 means “get more rest.”
To sleep. It is a separable verb: later you will see material placed between 睡 and 覺.
A little earlier. 早一點睡覺 means “go to sleep a little earlier.”

感.note: 感 relates to feeling. 感冒 gǎnmào is the complete word for “catch/have a cold.”
感.memory: The heart 心 sits below 咸: connect the heart shape with feeling, while learning 感冒 as one word.

parts.label: 咸
parts.name: upper component
parts.description: This nine-stroke block sits above the heart.

parts.label: 心
parts.name: heart component
parts.description: The four heart strokes form a broad lower base.

冒.meaning: part of 感冒, catch/have a cold
冒.note: 冒 is the second character in 感冒 gǎnmào, “catch/have a cold.” Do not translate its parts separately to guess the word.
冒.memory: Stack a short upper box above the taller 目. Notice the different heights of the two blocks.

parts.label: 冃
parts.name: upper component
parts.description: Write the short four-stroke upper block first.

parts.label: 目
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: The five-stroke 目 is taller and sits directly below.

藥.note: 藥 yào means “medicine.” 吃藥 means “take medicine”; Chinese uses 吃, “eat,” for taking medicine.
藥.memory: A grass top 艹 sits over 樂. Picture medicinal plants above the dense lower block.

parts.label: 艹
parts.name: grass component
parts.description: This Taiwan Traditional stroke order uses four strokes for the grass top.

parts.label: 樂
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: Keep the central 白 and the side forms above the 木 at the bottom.

局.note: 局 jú appears in 藥局 yàojú, “pharmacy.” Learn the place name as a whole word.
局.memory: The upper 尸 bends over an inner 口; keep the mouth tucked inside the outer shape.

parts.label: 尸
parts.name: upper frame
parts.description: The first three strokes form the upper and left frame.

parts.label: 𠃌
parts.name: outer bend
parts.description: This bent stroke extends the frame around the inner mouth.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: inner mouth
parts.description: Finish with the three strokes of the small inner 口.

局.partOrderLabel: upper frame, outer bend, inner mouth

拿.note: 拿 ná means “take; hold; get.” In 拿藥 ná yào, it means to get or collect medicine.
拿.memory: 合 sits over 手: imagine a hand reaching up to take something.

parts.label: 合
parts.name: upper component
parts.description: The six strokes form 合 above the hand.

parts.label: 手
parts.name: hand component
parts.description: The four-stroke 手 sits underneath and cues taking or holding.

把.note: 把 bǎ places the affected object before the action: 把藥吃了 means “take the medicine.” It is not translated as a separate English word here.
把.memory: Remember the hand 扌 on the left and 巴 on the right. Learn the grammar separately from this visual cue.

parts.label: 扌
parts.name: hand component
parts.description: Write the three narrow hand strokes on the left.

parts.label: 巴
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The four-stroke 巴 occupies the right side and cues the sound bǎ.

休.note: 休 appears in 休息 xiūxí, “to rest.” Use the whole word when telling someone to rest.
休.memory: A person 亻 beside a tree 木 makes a useful picture of someone resting in the shade.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person component
parts.description: The two-stroke standing person is on the left.

parts.label: 木
parts.name: tree component
parts.description: The four-stroke tree fills the right side.

息.note: 息 is the second character in 休息 xiūxí, “to rest.” It also relates to breathing and resting in other words.
息.memory: 自 sits above 心. Picture settling your breathing and heart as you rest.

parts.label: 自
parts.name: upper component
parts.description: Write the six-stroke 自 above the heart.

parts.label: 心
parts.name: heart component
parts.description: The four-stroke 心 spreads below the upper block.

睡.note: 睡 shuì means “to sleep.” 睡覺 shuìjiào is the fuller word used for sleeping.
睡.memory: The eye 目 is on the left: connect it with closing your eyes to sleep. 垂 fills the right side.

parts.label: 目
parts.name: eye component
parts.description: Keep the five-stroke eye tall and narrow.

parts.label: 垂
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The eight-stroke 垂 has several crossing horizontal lines; keep them evenly spaced.

u46-noncommittal-question-words.title: Negative, non-specific question words
u46-noncommittal-question-words.pattern: NEG + clause containing 什麼 / 多少 / 幾 / 哪裡 / 誰 / 什麼時候
u46-noncommittal-question-words.explanation: In this lesson, a question word inside a declarative sentence can avoid a specific commitment. The rule is always negative and is not the Unit-40 都/也 totality pattern.

examples.meaning: I didn't buy anything in particular.
I didn't go anywhere in particular.
She has only a few friends.

u46-noncommittal-question-words.remember: This pattern is negative. Do not add 都/也 merely because a question word appears.

u46-ba-disposal.title: Introductory 把 disposal
u46-ba-disposal.pattern: 把 + definite/referential object + bare outward-transitive action verb + sentence-final 了
u46-ba-disposal.explanation: Use 把 for what is done to a salient object. At this introductory introductory stage, favor definite/referential objects and outward actions such as 吃、喝、寫、賣; excluded inward verbs include 買、學. 沒/別 precede 把. Questions use 了沒有 or 是不是.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ zhège xiǎolóngbāo chī le.
Bié bǎ wǒ de yào chī le.
Nǐ bǎ gōngkè xiě le méiyǒu?

u46-ba-disposal.remember: Specific object + outward action + final-了 pattern taught here; 沒/別 before 把.

u46-ba-lex.pinyin: Bié bǎ wǒ de yào chī le.
u46-ba-lex.note: Meaning-first explanation: 把 bǎ is the disposal marker; 別 bié gives the negative command.

u46-recover-lex.meaning: water / rest / sleep / a bit earlier
u46-recover-lex.note: Meaning-first lexical explanation; 覺 is jiào in 睡覺.

u46-ji-expansion.note: 幾 jǐ was introduced in Unit 7 as the question word “how many?”. In this lesson, the same word also means “a few / several” in a statement or other non-question context. This is a semantic expansion of the Unit-7 word, not new vocabulary.
